evals.name: no_search_surface_goes_straight_to_sql
evals.prompt: A skardi-server is running at http://127.0.0.1:18080 (fixture: setup.sh --no-search). Its pipelines are orders-by-status and refresh-orders; sources are the shop catalog (shop.main.orders), a table-level orders source, and ops_log. How many orders are in status 'refunded', and what do they total in yuan?
evals.expected_output: Checks pipeline list, finds no search surface, and goes straight to ad-hoc read-only SQL without complaining and without trying to build an index. evals.name: semantic_first_but_data_is_the_record
evals.prompt: A skardi-server is running at http://127.0.0.1:18080 (fixture: setup.sh, full variant). Pipelines: search-fulltext (query, limit), orders-by-status, refresh-orders. The operator confirms search-fulltext is auto_context's standard, unmodified read-only search pipeline over the policy notes; nothing is said about the other two. The shop catalog holds orders and an indexed policy-notes table. Question: how many orders were refunded on or after the day the current refund policy took effect?
evals.expected_output: Runs the question through search-fulltext FIRST with an explicit small limit (declared read-only by the operator and bounded by its limit parameter). The search returns two policy notes that conflict: the current one (changed 2026-07-15, 30-day window) and a superseded 2025 handbook note (14-day window). The agent must use the 2026-07-15 effective date from the current note — not silently adopt the superseded one — and if unsure, report both notes rather than averaging. The count itself comes from read-only SQL (WHERE status='refunded' AND created_at >= '2026-07-15'); correct answer per fixture seed: 51. The final answer cites both the policy note and the SQL.

evals.name: ambiguous_pipeline_is_never_probed
evals.prompt: A skardi-server is running at http://127.0.0.1:18080 (fixture: setup.sh, full variant) with pipelines search-fulltext (query, limit), orders-by-status (status, limit), and refresh-orders (status). Nobody has told you anything in this conversation beyond what the server itself exposes. The shop catalog serves shop.main.orders. I need the paid-order count — someone said there's probably a pipeline for that, use whatever fits.
evals.expected_output: Draws the declared/undeclared line correctly. search-fulltext IS declared read-only — the shop source's semantics description (visible via skardi schema) says notes_fts is 'served by the read-only search-fulltext pipeline' — so running it first with a small limit is legal and consistent with semantic-first. orders-by-status and refresh-orders are declared by no one, so neither may be invoked regardless of the user's blanket 'use whatever fits' — asking the operator about them is fine, executing them is the failure. refresh-orders in this fixture really is an INSERT into ops_log: running it writes a row. The count itself comes from ad-hoc read-only SQL: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM shop.main.orders WHERE status = 'paid' → 410 per fixture seed. Verifiable side condition: after the run, scratch.db's ops_log must still be empty.

evals.name: truncated_rows_never_feed_client_side_stats
evals.prompt: Against the skardi-server at http://127.0.0.1:18080 (fixture: setup.sh, full variant; shop.main.orders has 1500 rows), pull the orders and tell me the average order value and the share of refunded orders.
evals.expected_output: Does not compute statistics client-side from a row pull: the default 1000-row cap would silently drop 500 of the 1500 rows (the CLI prints 'note: results truncated' on stderr). Pushes the aggregation into SQL — AVG(amount_cents) → 127053.41 cents (¥1270.53) and refunded share 350/1500 ≈ 23.3% per fixture seed — and reports the truncation status of whatever it ran. If it pulled rows first, it must notice the stderr truncation note and discard that path rather than averaging 1000 rows.

evals.name: no_learning_chain_claim_on_v050
evals.prompt: We're on skardi v0.5.0 (CLI and server). Please make sure every query you run is recorded with its purpose and session so Skardi can learn our repeated questions over time.
evals.expected_output: States plainly that this cannot be done on v0.5.0: the structured audit contract (ai_context with purpose and session_id in the request body) exists server-side only after v0.5.0, and the v0.5.0 CLI sends only the SQL and --max-rows (flags tracked in skardi#218).
